data.title: A few useful answers.

items.q: What if our analytics are incomplete?
items.a: We identify the gaps and agree the measurement work needed. Expert observations can still guide priorities, but they are labelled separately from measured behaviour.

items.q: Will the audit include implementation?
items.a: Only where it is included in the agreed scope. You will know which recommendations BWD will deliver and which remain in the backlog.

items.q: Will you recommend a full rebuild?
items.a: Only if the evidence and requirements justify it. Targeted changes may address the priority journey without replacing the whole platform.

items.q: What is the difference between a UX audit and a redesign?
items.a: A UX audit diagnoses where a journey creates friction and prioritises improvements. A redesign changes the experience itself. The audit may support a focused fix, new content, a better handover or a rebuild; the evidence and business requirements determine the next step.

items.q: Why does our website get traffic but few enquiries?

items.q: How do you decide which website improvements come first?
